question: A poison with a very high volume of distribution (Vd > 1 L/kg) will show high blood concentrations relative to tissue concentrations after absorption.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. A high Vd means extensive tissue distribution and LOW blood concentrations. High blood levels relative to tissues indicate a LOW Vd (e.g., lithium), where the poison remains largely in the vascular compartment and haemodialysis is effective.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect. A high Vd means the poison distributes extensively INTO tissues, leaving LOW blood concentrations — the poison is 'hiding' in peripheral compartments. This is why haemodialysis is ineffective for high-Vd poisons like digoxin.
